title: RPG Maker Key required to contribute to RMW forums: for your consideration.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
We have had an abundance of spam in recent months. And there are a number of ways we can combat some of the bot spam, of which would be recruiting a new mod that is typically active when others are asleep; but sometimes we get spam from not bots but just people who think RMW and our RM community is a place to market their skills and services but otherwise contribute nothing to the community.
Additionally, we have a number of people come to RMW forums who are asking for help with products that we have to tell them "due to the confusing nature of how
that
RM product was published, we cannot support it, despite being from the same franchise of software."
Well, funnily enough
@LionessPaladin
had made a one off joke that...well every time we bump into one of these kind of situations I keep thinking, "Actually, that joke would solve a lot of these problems."
What is it?
Well, on sign up, you'd need to provide a key or proof of purchase for any of the Makers in order to contribute to the forums.
This would be an automatic system that reduces the workload generated for our (wonderful) volunteer mods, would reduce the support questions our (wonderful) volunteer members have to turn away, and would reduce the unpleasant marketing people think this is a great place to do that on.
Is it all a win/win?
No, not necessarily.
There are users (in fact one just today) who come here asking which version they should buy, so obviously they don't have a key for it yet. It's an unfortunate loss that we cannot help them make that decision, but ultimately there are a number of available resources; from existing threads on the topic, to reddit, discord groups, and google searches - that will help them make that determination. So overall, not a huge loss.
There are, I am sure, technical hurdles to this as well. But I thought it would be good to seed the idea first. Technical issues can always be ironed out later once the people in charge consider this to be a good idea.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
So one idea that popped into my head to handle the Steam users would actually not to be the activation key for the software, but instead basically issue a "support key".
If we are just spit balling ideas here for things that we all know will never ever get implemented, then I think this pretty much solves that technical hurdle. It does however create the new hurdle of - if we want these keys to be easily found - requiring all the Makers to be updated.
Basically, the way I'd imagine that working is that the support key is a wholly new generated key. You would just go to help -> show support key and it would show you the key for activating your account on RMW. RMW itself could just have a mini tutorial at sign up to help users find it too.
Alternatively, the key could just be a generated text file that gets placed in the downloaded folder. A little less elegant, but wouldn't require updating the Makers themselves.
And to also make another point clear, I would imagine if this were to be implemented, it shouldn't be applied retroactively. Basically, accounts that are here now get to stay; lucky you! But new sign ups would require the support key.
One other thing this might assist with is weeding out some of the pirates as well. If the support key was generated at the time of download, then pirates wouldn't have a legitimate support key to use, basically locking them out of using RMW.
As usual, I feel I should repeat the point I have already made in that this is obviously not fool proof. It would only
reduce
but not prevent any of these actors, including pirates. But hey, if a pirate decides to spend $2 on XP to get a support key, that's $2 more made from a pirate than without. This really applies to any scenario. Like if a spammer or marketer wants to use the forum, then they at least need to pay to use this space right? So at least if they are coming here to make money, at least Komodo makes a little kickback when they buy up a slew of XP keys to do their marketing. Better then spammers wasting bandwidth because the barrier to entry is $0
